identity.title: Flow Matching with General Discrete Paths: A Kinetic-Optimal Perspective

problem.claim: Design discrete-space generative models based on continuous-time Markov chains while choosing suitable probability paths.

gap.claim: Discrete diffusion and flow model design is described as less understood than the continuous-space case, with much prior work centered on simple masking.

contributions.claim: A construction framework for discrete generative models that permits arbitrary discrete probability paths.
Velocity formulas based on symmetric kinetic-energy optimization that decouple probability paths from velocities.
A mixture probability-path construction reported to optimize symmetric kinetic energy in the discrete case.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their approach is the first to allow arbitrary discrete probability paths, or corruption processes, in this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical validation across text generation, inorganic material generation, and image generation.
In text generation, the authors report that kinetic-optimal mixture paths outperform the mask construction.
For visual data, the authors report using domain-specific probability-path constructions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper identifies limited understanding of discrete-space generative-model design and the dominance of masking.
It introduces arbitrary discrete probability paths within continuous-time Markov-chain models.
It derives path-independent velocity formulas through symmetric kinetic-energy optimization and identifies a kinetic-optimal mixture construction.
It reports multimodal validation, text gains over masking, and domain-specific visual paths.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates the probability path from the velocity and allows path choice using domain knowledge.

lessons.interpretation: A model description can expose design choices as modular components, making domain assumptions explicit.
lessons.application: When presenting a generative-model variant, define the data-dependent path separately from the dynamics or parameterization, then state which component is optimized or selected.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the path and dynamics are intrinsically coupled by the method or when no meaningful domain-specific path is available.

unknowns: No quantitative metrics, baselines beyond masking, dataset details, or statistical conditions are provided.
The abstract does not state the formal assumptions or proof details behind the kinetic-optimality claim.
The scope and comparative effect of the domain-specific visual constructions are not quantified.
